title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RUTHIE'S CORN
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Ruthie Vance, a feed store cashier from Mount Vernon, Ohio.
Her family's corn farm is a hundred years old. And her dad wanted to sell it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE LETTER
segments.quote: The only way to discover the limits of the possible is to go beyond them into the impossible.
segments.author: Arthur C. Clarke
lines: A storage-unit company offered Dad cash for the land.
Ruthie had a crazy idea. A corn maze. Dad spilled his coffee laughing.
But she remembered a line from the science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke:
The only way to discover the limits of the possible is to go beyond them into the impossible.
She asked Dad for one summer before he signed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE COW
segments.quote: Farming looks mighty easy when your plow is a pencil, and you're a thousand miles from the corn field.
segments.author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
lines: She drew a cow-shaped maze with forty dead ends.
Dad looked at it and quoted President Eisenhower:
Farming looks mighty easy when your plow is a pencil, and you're a thousand miles from the corn field.
So she put the pencil down, walked every row, and mowed it herself.
The cow came out looking like a potato. A potato with nice paths.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: OPENING DAY
segments.quote: Knowing trees, I understand the meaning of patience. Knowing grass, I can appreciate persistence.
segments.author: Hal Borland
lines: Opening day, she sold eleven tickets. Four were cousins.
By lunch, she wanted to quit. Then she read Grandpa's barn calendar, from the nature writer Hal Borland:
Knowing trees, I understand the meaning of patience. Knowing grass, I can appreciate persistence.
Corn doesn't grow in a day either. So she opened every weekend, rain or shine.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE REAL CROP
segments.quote: The ultimate goal of farming is not the growing of crops, but the cultivation and perfection of human beings.
segments.author: Masanobu Fukuoka
lines: By October, cars lined the road. A grumpy trucker got lost and came out laughing.
Her boss lent her a book by Japanese farmer Masanobu Fukuoka:
The ultimate goal of farming is not the growing of crops, but the cultivation and perfection of human beings.
So she added hayrides, a bonfire, and free cider for anyone who came out still arguing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE OFFER
segments.quote: That man is the richest whose pleasures are the cheapest.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: Then came a bigger offer. Dad had his pen out.
Ruthie watched families laughing over three-dollar marshmallows, and thought of Henry David Thoreau:
That man is the richest whose pleasures are the cheapest.
She took Dad's pen and handed him a flashlight. Walk it first, she said.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: DAD GETS LOST
segments.quote: Every now and then a man's mind is stretched by a new idea or sensation, and never shrinks back to its former dimensions.
segments.author: Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.
lines: Dad came out two hours later, corn silk in his eyebrows, grinning.
He quoted the writer Oliver Wendell Holmes:
Every now and then a man's mind is stretched by a new idea or sensation, and never shrinks back to its former dimensions.
He tore up the offer. Next year's maze is shaped like his face. Moustache and all.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Try the impossible. Walk the field. Be patient. Grow people. Count cheap joys. Let your mind stretch.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Try the impossible. Get into the field. Be patient. Grow people. Count cheap joys. Let your mind stretch.
I once got lost in a hedge maze. The hedges were four feet tall.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
